pages.text: The thing a training line fears is not stopping — it is $(bold)losing power mid-run$(). The $(item)UPS Power Distribution Array$() exists for exactly that: it float-charges while the grid is healthy, takes over the load when it browns out, and buys a nearby pretraining cluster $(bold)60 seconds (1200 ticks)$() of buffer.$(br2)It $(bold)generates nothing$() — it only returns what it stored.

pages.title: 5×4×3 Structure & Float Charge
pages.text: $(li)$(#0E7490)y=0..1$(): the battery banks of $(item)UPS Battery Casing$(); the controller sits front-centre on the second layer at $(bold)(2, 1, 0)$() with the Energy and Maintenance Hatches on the same layer.$(li)$(#0E7490)y=2$(): the bus-bar service walkway between the two banks, $(item)Solid Steel Machine Casing$() in the middle.$(li)$(#0E7490)y=3$(): a $(item)Steel Frame$() roof girder carrying the cable tray.$(br2)Once powered it float-charges at $(bold)4096 EU/t$() into a $(bold)4,000,000 EU$() bank.

pages.title: What 60 Seconds Actually Buys
pages.text: The moment the grid drops, any pretraining cluster within $(bold)12 blocks$() draws from the UPS, up to $(bold)8192 EU/t$() of discharge. Those 60 seconds buy:$(li)The running batch keeps stepping, so $(bold)checkpoints keep landing$().$(li)If the grid returns inside the window, training $(bold)resumes from the most recent checkpoint$() with no lost progress.$(li)If the bank drains first, the unsaved progress is cleared and the run falls back to that checkpoint.$(br2)The UPS itself never loses charge on a power cut — its stored EU lives in the save.
